shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures fell to their lowest level since August 17 on Monday, extending losses for a fourth straight session, as the yen held near seven-month highs and rubber demand softened.($1 = 153.7000 yen)($1 = 6.7057 yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures fell to their lowest level since August 17 on Monday, extending losses for a fourth straight session, as the yen held near seven-month highs and rubber demand softened.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
was down 6.3 yen, or 1.46%, at 424.7 yen ($2.76) per kg as of 0159 GMT.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
fell 410 yuan, or 2.12%, to 18,930 yuan ($2,822.97) per metric ton.
The most active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) slumped 615 yuan, or 3.92%, to 15,090 yuan per metric ton.

Prices were weighed down by a stronger yen ahead of a possible Bank of Japan rate hike and potential currency intervention by the Ministry of Finance, with carry trades also unwinding in the dollar-yen pair, Japan Exchange Group said in a report on Monday.
was at 153.49 per U.S. dollar, not far from the seven-month high of 152.89 it touched last week as fresh signs emerged of market sentiment on the Asian currency changing.
A stronger currency makes yen-denominated assets less affordable to overseas buyers.
share gauge fell sharply on Monday, dragged down by technology shares after leaders of major AI companies called for a slowdown in development.

The capacity utilisation rate of sample all-steel tyre companies in top rubber consumer China was at 65.71% last week, falling 0.23 percentage points week-on-week and 1.51 percentage points from the previous year, according to data from Longzhong Information.

Average purchases of natural rubber by tyre manufacturers declined this week amid rising raw material costs, with most companies remaining in a state of production control, said analysts from Chaos Ternary Futures Research Institute.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for November delivery (STFX6) last traded at 236 U.S. cents per kg, down 2.4%.
